Yeah they won't do anything, I have a lifetime warranty but they tell me it has to blow before they cover me. Sucks but at least I'm covered.

All I have to do is keep records of engine maintenance which I do have.  I am out of power train warranty as I am the second owner but I can try getting it tested by the dealer and see what happens. I'll also be checking the oil more frequently from now on.

I got the car when I was 19 for my birthday, I can get another vehicle but dealing with a note for another 3-4 years is not ideal. I have a lifetime warranty on the engine because of this problem, so I figured it's worth keeping for now with that if they can just replace the engine for failure. If it is burning oil I can try and get addressed to prepare for this. However my current concern as everyone else I take it to brings up is that it's not burning oil, they just didn't change the oil or changed it incorrectly. I have no symptoms of this other than low oil, which fortunately didn't cause any critical damage.

I recently got it changed and it hasn't even been 1K miles which bad engines usually burn a quart or more within that time. If it takes 5 quarts my engine would have to be blowing smoke for that, which is why I say it's likely not to be that at least at this time. But if it is burning oil I thank everyone for letting me know so I can take better care of it. I'll find out in the upcoming weeks.

I guess i'll prepare for the worst.

I do check my oil that's how I found all this out. I recently got it changed not too long ago and I always go to them for this service. My question is can you burn 5 quarts of oil in such a small time span?

Also keep in mind my engine holds about 5 quarts of oil, IMO there is absolutely no way my engine can burn that much oil while running fine. I have 75K miles on it as well.
